What exact minimum readable range do both frame_get_chunk (c-blosc2/blosc/frame.c:1740) and frame_get_lazychunk (c-blosc2/blosc/frame.c:1830) require after get_coffset returns a nonnegative offset, and would validating header_len + offset + BLOSC2_CHUNK_CBYTES + sizeof(int32_t) <= frame->len inside get_coffset preserve sparse-frame semantics?

The supplied ASan report shows frame_get_lazychunk computing frame->cframe + header_len + offset and reading a 32-bit cbytes field out of bounds. get_coffset currently rejects only decoded offsets greater than frame->len and allows negative special chunk values. The organizer explicitly asks validation to account for header_len, integer overflow, and enough remaining bytes for the chunk header/field before returning the offset. I am determining whether the check should apply universally or only to contiguous frames because sparse offsets may identify separate files rather than positions relative to the frame.
